goal: Split Postgres.js pools so heavy dashboard/KPI reads bulkhead off the write path (dedicated Vercel read client), raise the Railway worker pool to cover merged BullMQ concurrency, and surface a worker pool-wait/saturation metric in queue-health.
non_goals: No schema change / no migration (pure client + config + observability).
No read replica or second database URL — the read client points at the same DATABASE_POOL_URL (bulkhead = separate pool instance, not separate DB).
No alerting on pool-wait this ticket — queue-health payload observability only; HealthAlertPoller integration is a documented follow-up.
No change to worker BullMQ concurrency values (gen 5, ingest 5, notif 4, pub 4 stay; this ticket sizes the POOL to them).
No switch of settings/write pages or OAuth-handshake routes onto the read client — read-only dashboard/KPI paths only.
No code change to the pool-max DEFAULT (stays 10) — raising Railway is env-only (DB_POOL_MAX=20), so Vercel is never accidentally raised.

Does NOT move the heavy fan-out read routes (dashboard route ~14-wave, aggregate ~8-wave, agent-team) onto sqlRead — their concurrency exceeds a right-sized read pool and they carry the pre-existing #505 pipelining-wedge risk, which stays OWNED by the #505 Vercel pipelining audit (differential-repro required). Only wedge-safe small-fan-out reads (KPI ≤6 concurrent, draft-status ≤2 concurrent / up to 4 reads) move.
Does NOT claim application_name gives pooler attribution — ADR 0007 proved Supavisor flattens it to 'Supavisor'; it is kept only as harmless client intent.
The read bulkhead isolates only LOCAL postgres.js client slots (sqlRead shares the same Supavisor backend pool as sql — same URL/user/db/mode); it does not isolate backend DB capacity.

SURFACE AMENDMENT (user-approved 2026-07-19): introducing sqlRead exposed a tenant-scope AUDIT blind spot — scripts/ci/tenant-scope-audit.ts only recognized the `sql` tag, so sqlRead-tagged tenant-scoped reads (accounts/responses) dropped out of isolation-audit coverage. Fix (in-scope for correct pool wiring): extractSqlTagNames recognizes sqlRead as a SQL-tag source + regression test. scripts/ci/tenant-scope-audit.ts added to edit surface.
user_visible_behavior: GET /internal/queue-health response gains a `pool` field: { waitMs, timedOut, saturating, max } (best-effort; null on genuine probe error; timedOut:true (=> saturating:true) when the single-flight reserve() probe hits its timeout — waitMs is then a censored lower bound).
Admin jobs panel surfaces the worker pool-wait/saturation signal (waitMs, shown as `>=` when timedOut) alongside per-queue depth + backlog.
No customer-facing behavior change; KPI + past-replies/draft-status reads served from the dedicated read pool (identical responses).
invariants: #15: the second (read) pool is wired at composition roots ONLY (route handlers / server components pass the read client); domain modules keep receiving sql as a parameter and never import db/server.
#1: Vercel stays UI-only; the pool-wait metric lives on the worker (queue-health is a Railway-side endpoint Vercel fetches server-side).
Tenant isolation unchanged — read client runs the same account_id/business_id-scoped queries; only the connection pool differs.
Shutdown close-order contract preserved: the pool-wait probe never leaks a reserved connection (release even if our timeout already fired).
postgres.js dedicated-client base config stays single-owner (BASE_POSTGRES_OPTIONS): prepare:false, idle/lifetime/connect timeouts.
edge_cases: reserve() probe on a saturated pool WAITS — bound it with a timeout; a timeout is reported as saturating:true (not null).
reserve() that resolves AFTER our timeout must still .release() — attach release to the underlying promise so no reserved connection leaks.
reserve() rejects (connection error) → pool:null, must not regress the primary `queues` signal (mirror backlog degrade-to-null).
The pool-wait probe briefly holds ONE connection (immediate release) — negligible added pressure, acceptable.

sqlRead is a module-level singleton imported by the worker too, but postgres.js is lazy — the worker never queries it (zero connections there). It STILL gets an explicit closer: closeAllPostgresClients ends sqlRead best-effort (alongside dedicated closers), while sql.end() stays awaited directly so its rejection still propagates (shutdown contract preserved).
sqlRead max is code-FLOORED at WEDGE_SAFE_READ_MIN=8 (DB_READ_POOL_MAX can only raise, never set below) so a mis-set env cannot reintroduce the #505 fan-out wedge.

Capacity ceiling (MEASURED): Nano/free tier, max_connections=60, reserved_connections=0 → 57 usable backend sessions; Max-Clients ≈200. Idle backend sessions also consume slots. Vercel budget: worker20+health2+isolates×(write3+read8) ≤ 200 → ≤16 warm isolates. DB_POOL_MAX=20 is a ceiling-aware starting value blessed only by the hard staging gate (pg_stat_activity + Supavisor pool_size).
Vercel serverless has no explicit shutdown — sqlRead idle-timeout-reaps like the existing sql singleton (consistent, no closer).
existing_patterns_to_follow: createDedicatedPostgresClient + closeAllPostgresClients (src/lib/db/server.ts) — the health-poller bulkhead precedent for a separate pool.
queue-health `backlog` best-effort pattern (worker/internal/queue-health.ts): dependency-injected getter, withTimeout-bounded, degrade-to-null, never regress `queues`.
KPI read-cache fail-open block (src/lib/kpi/service.ts) — read path already param-injected (sql: Sql) + cache-fronted.
DB_POOL_MAX env-tunable pool sizing (readPoolMax) — add DB_READ_POOL_MAX in the same shape.
tests_to_add: pool-wait probe: free pool → { waitMs~0, timedOut:false, saturating:false, max }; releases the reserved connection once.
pool-wait probe: timeout → timedOut:true, saturating:true, waitMs=timeoutMs (censored lower bound); late-resolving reserve still released (no leak).
pool-wait probe: single-flight REGRESSION (#10) — a timed-out call does NOT release the latch; the second call reuses the still-pending reserve() (reserve() count stays 1); resolution releases once.
pool-wait probe: concurrent probes over a pending reservation share ONE reserve().
pool-wait probe: genuine reserve() rejection is re-thrown → handler maps to pool:null; primary queues signal unaffected.
pool-wait probe: a rejecting reserve() with 2 concurrent awaiters emits NO unhandledRejection (latch cleanup is rejection-safe — the worker crash-net would otherwise fatally exit).
queue-health handler: `pool` { waitMs, timedOut, saturating, max } present in 200 payload; degrades independently of `backlog` and `queues`.
server.ts: sqlRead is a distinct client from sql, with options.max>=8 and statement_timeout=8000.
server.ts: DB_READ_POOL_MAX=1 is floored to WEDGE_SAFE_READ_MIN (wedge-safety invariant).
server.ts: closeAllPostgresClients invokes sqlRead.end() AND a rejecting sql.end() still propagates.
KPI + past-replies/draft-status read routes: composition root passes sqlRead, not the write singleton.
